question: Does industry MEDIAN_ocfYieldProxy carry information about future H126 industry-minus-069500.KS return AFTER controlling for REL_MOM_126, PIT market beta and TOP1_CAP_SHARE, on one common industry-date set?
outcomeAccess: NONE. Only the input columns listed in inputColumns are read from the panel. No rel_*, status_*, entry*/exit*, status or reason column is read. Labels are synthetic.

missing.PIT_MARKET_BETA: Not a column of the panel. No beta is filled or imputed. Design K2 omits it and is an UPPER BOUND on feasibility: adding a control can only remove a degree of freedom and can only shrink the joint mask. Design K3 adds a synthetic, persistent, label-irrelevant control so the df it consumes is counted.

maturityRule: A date is usable for horizon H only if its synthetic window ends on or before the last panel date (calendar position only).
statistic: Per-date partial Spearman: within-date average ranks of feature, label and controls; feature ranks and label ranks residualised by OLS on [1, control ranks]; Pearson correlation of the residuals. Date-equal mean over usable dates.

inference.registered: One-sided self-normalised t (Lobato 2001 / Shao 2010) on the time-ordered per-date series; fixed-b limit critical value computed in this module from IID N(0,1) paths (seed 20261031).
inference.multiplicity: Holm over the two horizon slots at familywise 0.05: the primary first step is one-sided alpha 0.025. The power reported is power of that first step, which is an UPPER BOUND on Holm power.
inference.liberalReference: Newey-West t, Bartlett lag = horizon weeks, normal critical value. Known to over-reject under this overlap; reported only to show the verdict does not hinge on the conservative test.

dgp.label: y[t,i] = c * Hw * s[t,i] + sum_{w=t+1}^{t+Hw} u[w,i], where s is the within-date standardised residual of the real feature rank on the real control ranks, u is drawn on the full 610-date x 14-industry grid so overlapping windows share shocks exactly as calendar positions dictate, and c = rho / sqrt(Hw * (1 - rho^2)) makes the per-date Pearson correlation of s and y equal rho.
dgp.syntheticBeta: K3 only: AR(1) on the weekly grid, phi 0.98, unit stationary variance, drawn once per cell; it does not enter y.

decisionRule.economicallyMeaningfulRationale: Marginal anatomy reading: IC +0.136 with a +4.7pp H126 top-minus-bottom tercile gap. A conditional rho of 0.10 is roughly a 3.5pp/126d tercile gap, about 7pp/yr gross long-short and about half that long-only against the ETF, before costs. Smaller effects cannot pay for a sector-rotation book; larger ones are not a reasonable prior for an increment over momentum.
decisionRule.GO: H126 K2 IID_NORMAL registered-test power at rho = 0.10 >= 0.80 AND the registered test's size at rho = 0 <= 0.0375 in every noise cell.
decisionRule.NO_GO: Anything else. K2 is the most favourable design available: if it fails, the real design (K3 with a real beta mask and an outcome-validity mask that removes terminated-name cohorts) cannot pass, so no outcome is to be read and no beta needs to be built for this question.
decisionRule.noRescue: No change of horizon, minimum cross-section, feature, control set, test, effect threshold or sample after this file is committed.
